TO your sister-in-law.

1st: I'm sorry for your pain. It isn't your fault. The system is broken beyond repair. You can't be part of the solution ... so get out.

That being said: I'm in Texas and I would NEVER send my kids to a public school. Private school, home school, anything beside the failing system that is public education. My wife and I make significant sacrifices to keep our kids out of the school system. To be blunt: we care about our kids too much to send them to a public school, or as I call it: an indoctrination camp.

And, it isn't the teachers. It's the system. It's the nature of the beast. The leveling systems are designed to create uniformity and conformity. I don't want my kids to conform or be uniform. I want them to be able to think for themselves. I want them to be, for lack of a better word, dangerous .

Further, the education system caters to the lowest common denominator, not the best and the brightest. I refuse to let my children be dragged down by the lowest common denominator.

We send our kids to a 3 day / week school and home school 2 days. My wife has a master's in education so her skills are rather underutilized in the home school role but she wouldn't want it any other way. Their classroom teachers love the kids and their kids love the teachers. I support their classroom teachers 100%. If my kid ever had a conflict with the teacher, I'd side with the teacher in a heart beat. But, that has never happened.

The school has the freedom to be selective. There is enough of hurdle (cost + time) to make the school self selective. To go to this school parents have to want it. This might sound crazy to hear, but I can comfortably say: there are no bad kids (or parents) at the school. Sure, some kids do stupid things but there is a distinct lack of evil in the school. I'd be completely comfortable with my kids spending time in any of the other kids homes.

Bottom line: if you are a good teacher, then your soul isn't worth the cost of public education. Take a pay cut and find an alternative education system. They exist and are amazing. They are growing like crazy (home schooling grew by double digits over the last ~5 years.) Awesome things are happening in education but you wouldn't know it being in the public school system.
